headline: Proteomics search methods extend to modifications, proteoforms and blind spots in peptide coverage
label: Proteomics Search Space Benchmarks
summary: Six items reflect pressure on how MS search spaces are defined, from modification combinations to peptide coverage biases, with new models and tools.
synthesis: The common thread is widening and constraining what a search can identify, then testing the assignments. MS Andrea scores combinations of PTMs per PSM using sequence tags in open searches, outperforming MSFragger and Sage. OligoFragger constrains modified-oligonucleotide searches with spectrum-graph fragment evidence to improve FDR-controlled identification. mE-DIA pairs multi-enzyme library-free DIA with proteoform inference, raising protein IDs by 30%. SeekNSee adds traceable, rule-level scoring for proteotypic peptide selection. A reanalysis of public data finds basic-pI peptides depleted (OR 0.45), pointing to coverage bias. π-SPECFormer, pre-trained on 291M spectra, targets de novo sequencing, clustering and modification detection. Newer than the prior emphasis on database filtering is the focus on proteoform resolution, foundation models and systematic coverage gaps.
